title: 0003 天牢0004 特殊的犯人
content_zh:
“地字还是人字？”既然前面的基础没打好，洪涛也不想马上翻脸，先忍着吧。
“嘿嘿嘿，这次可是好差事，天字号！赶紧收拾好吃饭的家伙什，不要让吴校尉多等！”兄弟俩眼中不由自主露出几分幸灾乐祸的光芒，嬉皮笑脸的说着风凉话。
“……”洪涛没说话，心里把他们祖宗十八代都挨个骂了个遍，头也不回的向地牢走去。
天字号的案犯最少，但麻烦最多。能被关进来的在外面都是呼风唤雨之辈，即便落了难也不可小觑。倒不是说他们还能还手，而是未来不可估量。
下手重了，万一人家获得了皇帝的宽恕，或者戴罪立功啥的，有朝一日出去了保不齐要想办法报复。就算被处死了，人家的亲朋故旧会不会有想法呢？
下手轻了，被同僚和上司发现也是罪过。而怎么才算下手合适，行刑力士们一般是判断不出来的，只能靠上司点拨。
问题就出在这里了，吴校尉和自己一样是个没什么根基、不太受上司青睐、只会干活的闷葫芦。指望他点拨自己，还不如扔铜板信命呢。
为什么要把这个工作交给吴校尉，其他两位当值校尉又忙不迭的离开，这里面的隐情就不得不让人起疑心了。
按照洪涛的鸡贼算计，怕不是巧合。很显然聪明人都在有意无意的躲，可又不能不干活，于是自己和吴校尉就成了冤大头。
是不是就无法应对了呢？也不是，作为行刑力士其实也背不上太多责任。就算囚犯或者其家属想报复，那也得能进得来镇妖殿才成。
自己成年累月都不带出去的，吃喝用度连带居所都在镇妖殿的公廨内，总不会有人在外面傻等一辈子吧。所以该怎么下手就怎么下手，一切按照诏狱的明文规定办就行了。
至于说结果咋样，爱咋样咋样呗。审不出口供的例子比比皆是，不缺这一个。更复杂的问题自然有大脑袋去琢磨，轮不到行刑力士多操心。
“校尉大人，卑职都准备好了！”来到地字号刑房把能用上的刑具装进箱子背着，刚进入天字区牢房，头发花白的吴校尉已经站在通道口等候了。
“嗯，去刑房干活吧！”老校尉也没废话，随口吩咐了一句转身就向外走。
“校尉大人留步……今日是哪位书吏执笔？”
洪涛见状赶紧出声挽留，按照诏狱的规矩审讯是不能独立完成的，必须有人用刑、有人问话记录。既然吴校尉不想观摩，那就得指定一名书吏配合，否则自己该问什么都不知道。
“鲁王殿下有令，全程一人用刑、问话、记录，不可旁观窥探，你可听清楚了！”吴校尉停住脚步却没转身，特意大声宣读了命令，让通道中的所有工作人员都听到。
“属下听清楚了，一人用刑、一人问话、一人记录，总共三个人！”洪涛闻言心中顿感不妙，赶紧把命令重复了一遍。
鲁王，皇帝陛下的长子，掌管镇妖殿3年有余，从没来过诏狱，更没有给行刑力士直接下过令。看来今天的囚犯很可能是大人物，必须认真对待。
“……是一人用刑、问话、记录，任何人不准靠近三十步内，本官也一样！”吴校尉终于把头转了过来，眼神里充满了说不清道不明的含义，再次重复了一遍命令，然后就迈着大步走了，好像逃跑似的。

“我就日你们所有人嘴！”
这次洪涛终于听明白了，或者叫想明白了。不是三个人分工合作，而是一个人把审讯环节都包揽了，而且是镇妖殿最高领导鲁王的命令。
自己何德何能，能一个人干三个人的活儿？这尼玛就不是正常审讯，而是巨大的阴谋。问题是避无可避了，伸头是一刀，缩头还是一刀。
“那我问什么啊……”心中狠狠骂完，洪涛突然想起个关键问题。没有卷宗，连对方是谁、干了什么都不清楚，总不能逼问一生之中有没有做过恶吧。
“什么都不用问！”
吴校尉已经不见了踪影，就算听见也不打算回复。就在洪涛琢磨着是不是来个自伤自残脱离苦海时，门外走进了一个穿黑袍戴兜帽的身影。
看着来人，洪涛浑身汗毛都竖起来了，眼神不由自主地撇向了桌上的刑具。如果对方说的话很不靠谱，那就只能一命换一命了，临死也得拉上个垫背的。
“我叫杨玄翊，皇帝陛下长子，封鲁王！”来人停在门口，伸手摘下兜帽露出张年轻的脸。宽额头尖下巴，浓眉深目，薄唇紧闭，嘴角微微下垂，蓄有短须，表情严肃。
“鲁……镇妖殿西殿诏狱行刑力士洪涛见过殿下！”是不是不怒自威洪涛不清楚，一秒钟之后他就跪在地上了。鲁王啊，顶头顶头顶头的上司，人在屋檐下不得不低头。
“这是卷宗，你先看看，然后告诉本王有何感想！”鲁王没动地方，也没说平身，啪的一声，一本硬皮小册子掉在了洪涛面前。
“……遵命……”对这玩意洪涛有点眼熟，不是这个时代而是前几辈子。地方官员发往中央的奏本大概就是这个样子，而且里面不用官印。
“……属下很少出去，不太懂政务。”奏本不太长，只有三折，洪涛很快就看完了，仍旧没敢抬头，小声回答。
“看来有人在蒙蔽本王，他们都说你是此处最憨厚少言之人，如今却滑头的很。若是不想被扔进炼妖炉，最好重说一次，想好了再说！”
可惜这个模棱两可，说了和没说差不多的答案没有蒙混过关，还被鲁王抓住了小辫子。
“呃……殷城隍对当地百姓是造福，但对朝廷不一定是好官。”
眼见敷衍不过去，洪涛索性抬起上身改成了跪坐姿势，让与坚硬石头地面亲密接触的膝盖骨先舒服舒服，然后把真实想法讲了出来。
是不是会被扔进炼妖炉已经无所谓了，既然鲁王殿下驾临身边就不会缺少高手保护，临死拉个垫背的计划显然没什么成功的可能性。有道是人之将死其言也善，死到临头了还不敢说真话更憋屈！
奏本里到底写了什么内容呢？并不复杂，但很窝心。从6月份开始，河南、河北两路遭遇旱情，月余没有下雨，土地龟裂江河断流，眼看着再不想办法救灾秋粮就会颗粒无收。
此事如果放在正常朝代，除了准备赈灾之外朝廷也没什么办法可想。然而这个时代不同，各地都有城隍一职，由受皇帝册封的过世名人担任。
他们具备法力，除了可以在辖区范围内为百姓祛除鬼邪之外，还能呼风唤雨，不过需要消耗相对数量的香火。但最终是否施法降雨救灾的决定权不在城隍手里，而是需要皇帝下旨。

时任河南路卫辉县城隍殷云霄多次上表朝廷，陈述当地旱情之严重，民众之苦难，恳请皇帝下旨准许动用当地的香火施法降雨，可等了一个多月迟迟没有等到回复。
眼看着庄稼全都要被干死了，这位城隍爷知道圣旨无望，可又不甘心看着百姓饿殍遍地。牙一咬干脆剑走偏锋来了个欺上瞒下，谎称已经得到旨意，遂动用卫辉县城隍庙积攒的香火施法降雨。
按照他的想法，等旱情缓解之后再去各地寺庙道观和大族手里借些香火补上，这样既不耽误给朝廷缴纳香火税，又能让治下百姓度过天灾，不是两全其美乎。
content_en:
"The character for land or the character for people?" Since the previous foundation was not laid well, Hong Tao didn't want to fall out immediately, so he should endure it for now.
"Hehehehe, it's a good job this time, Tianzihao! Hurry up and pack up the people who are eating, don't let Captain Wu wait any longer!" The two brothers couldn't help but reveal a bit of schadenfreude in their eyes, and they said sarcastic remarks with playful smiles.
"..." Hong Tao said nothing, scolding all eighteen generations of their ancestors in his heart, and walked towards the dungeon without looking back.
Tianzihao has the fewest criminals, but the most troubles. Those who can be imprisoned are the people outside who can move the wind and rain. Even if they are in trouble, they should not be underestimated. It’s not that they can still fight back, but the future is unpredictable.
The attack is heavy. If someone is forgiven by the emperor, or if he or she is guilty or has made meritorious service, he will have to find a way to retaliate if he goes out one day and fails to protect himself. Even if he is executed, will his relatives and friends have any thoughts?
If you strike lightly, it will be a crime to be discovered by colleagues and superiors. Executioners generally cannot judge what is the right time to strike, and can only rely on their superiors' instructions.
The problem lies here. Like himself, Captain Wu is a boring gourd with no foundation, not very favored by his boss, and only knows how to work. If you expect him to enlighten you, you might as well throw a coin and trust your fate.
Why should this job be handed over to Lieutenant Wu, and the other two captains on duty left in a hurry? The hidden secret here has to make people suspicious.
According to Hong Tao's chicken thief's plan, I'm afraid it's not a coincidence. It was obvious that smart people were hiding intentionally or unintentionally, but they had to work, so he and Captain Wu became the ones who were taken advantage of.
Is it impossible to cope with it? No, as an executioner, you don't actually have too much responsibility. Even if the prisoners or their families want to take revenge, they must be able to enter the Demon Suppression Hall.
I haven't taken him out for months and months. My food, drinks and accommodation are all in the public house of the Demon Suppression Hall. There is no way anyone will be waiting outside for a lifetime. So just do whatever you want to do, and just follow the express provisions of the prison.
As for how the results are, let’s just say how you like them. There are many examples of cases where confessions cannot be made during trials, and this one is not lacking. Naturally, big brains should consider more complex issues, and it is not the executioner's turn to worry about them.
"Master Xiaowei, you are all ready for your humble duties!" When he arrived at the Dizihao torture room, he put the available torture instruments into boxes and carried them on his back. As soon as he entered the Tianzi District cell, the gray-haired Xiaowei Wu was already standing at the entrance of the passage waiting.
"Well, let's go to the execution room and work!" The old lieutenant didn't waste any words. He casually ordered and turned around and walked out.
"Master Xiaowei, please stay...which scribe is writing today?"
Upon seeing this, Hong Tao quickly spoke out to persuade him to stay. According to the rules of the prison, the interrogation cannot be completed independently. Someone must torture and record the interviews. Since Captain Wu doesn't want to observe, he has to designate a scribe to cooperate, otherwise he won't know what to ask.
"His Royal Highness King Lu has an order. One person is to torture, question, and record the entire process. No one is allowed to watch and spy. You must have heard clearly!" Captain Wu stopped but did not turn around. He read the order loudly so that all the staff in the passage could hear it.
"My subordinates heard it clearly. One person is to torture, one is to interrogate, and one is to record. There are three people in total!" Hong Tao suddenly felt bad when he heard this and quickly repeated the order.
King Lu, the eldest son of His Majesty the Emperor, has been in charge of the Demon Suppression Hall for more than three years. He has never been to the prison, nor has he given any direct orders to the executioners. It seems likely that today's prisoner is a big shot and must be taken seriously.
"... one person tortures, interrogates, and records. No one is allowed to come within thirty steps, including this officer!" Captain Wu finally turned his head, his eyes full of unexplainable meaning, repeated the order again, and then walked away with long strides, as if running away.
"I'm going to fuck all of you!"
This time Hong Tao finally understood, orI want to understand. Instead of three people dividing the work and cooperating, one person took over all the interrogation aspects, and it was the order of King Lu, the top leader of the Demon Suppression Hall.
How can I do the work of three people by myself? This is not a normal interrogation, but a huge conspiracy. The problem is unavoidable, extending one's head is a knife, and shrinking one's head is still a knife.
"Then what am I asking..." After cursing in his heart, Hong Tao suddenly remembered a key question. There is no file, and we don’t even know who the other party is or what he did. We can’t really ask him whether he has done any evil in his life.
"No need to ask anything!"
Colonel Wu has disappeared, and even if he hears it, he has no intention of replying. Just when Hong Tao was wondering if he could escape from his misery by injuring himself, a figure wearing a black robe and a hood walked in outside the door.
Looking at the person coming, the hair on Hong Tao's body stood up, and his eyes involuntarily turned to the torture instruments on the table. If what the other party says is unreliable, then you can only exchange one life for another, and you have to have someone to support you when you die.
"My name is Yang Xuanyi, His Majesty the Emperor's eldest son, King Feng Lu!" The visitor stopped at the door, reached out and took off his hood, revealing a young face. He has a wide forehead and pointed chin, thick eyebrows and deep eyes, thin lips tightly closed, slightly drooped corners of his mouth, a short beard, and a serious expression.
"Lu...Hong Tao, the executioner in the west hall of the Demon Suppression Hall, has seen your highness!" Hong Tao didn't know whether he was not angry or not, but he knelt on the ground a second later. King Lu, the boss with his head above his head has to bow his head under the eaves.
"This is the file. Take a look at it first and then tell me what you think!" King Lu didn't move or say anything. With a snap, a hard-cover booklet fell in front of Hong Tao.
"...As ordered..." This thing looked familiar to Hong Tao, not from this era but from previous lives. The memorial sent by local officials to the central government probably looks like this, and there is no official seal in it.
"... My subordinate rarely goes out and doesn't know much about government affairs." The memorial was not too long, only 30% of it. Hong Tao finished reading it quickly, but still did not dare to raise his head and answered in a low voice.
"It seems that someone is trying to deceive me. They all say that you are the most honest and honest person here who speaks few words, but now you are very cunning. If you don't want to be thrown into the demon refining furnace, you'd better say it again and think about it before you say it!"
It's a pity that this ambiguous answer, which was almost the same as being said or not, didn't get through, and King Lu caught him by the pigtails.
"Well... Yin Chenghuang is a blessing to the local people, but he may not be a good official to the court."
Seeing that he couldn't cope with it, Hong Tao simply raised his upper body and changed to a kneeling position to make his kneecaps, which were in close contact with the hard stone ground, comfortable first, and then spoke out his true thoughts.
It doesn't matter whether he will be thrown into the demon refining furnace or not. Since His Highness King Lu is by his side, there will be no shortage of expert protection. The plan to support him before death obviously has no chance of success. It is said that when a person is about to die, he can speak kindly, but when death is imminent, it is even more aggrieved that he dare not tell the truth!
What exactly is written in the memorial? Not complicated, but very heartwarming. Starting in June, Henan and Hebei provinces have been hit by drought. It hasn't rained for more than a month. The land is cracked and rivers have stopped flowing. It seems that if we don't find ways to provide disaster relief, there will be no autumn grain harvest.
If this matter were placed in a normal dynasty, the court would have nothing to do except prepare for disaster relief. However, this era is different. The position of City God exists everywhere, and it is held by deceased celebrities who have been canonized by the emperor.
They have magical power. In addition to being able to rid the people of ghosts and evil spirits within their jurisdiction, they can also call for wind and rain, but they need to consume a relatively large amount of incense. But in the end, the decision of whether to cast rain to provide disaster relief was not in the hands of the city god, but the emperor's decree.
At that time, Yin Yunxiao, the mayor of Weihui County in Henan Road, went to the court many times to state the severity of the local drought and the suffering of the people, and begged the emperor to issue an edict to use local incense to cast rain, but after waiting for more than a month, there was still no arrival.reply.
Seeing that all the crops were about to be dried up, the City God knew that the imperial edict was hopeless, but he was not willing to watch the people starve to death everywhere. He gritted his teeth and simply took a different approach and deceived the superiors and subordinates. He lied that he had obtained the decree and used the incense accumulated in the Chenghuang Temple in Weihui County to cast rain.
According to his idea, after the drought eased, he would go to various temples, Taoist temples and wealthy families to borrow some incense to replenish it. This would not delay paying the incense tax to the court, but also allow the people under his rule to survive the natural disaster. It was not the best of both worlds.
